title: Perfect complexes over a derived-complete ring are derived complete
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, let $I\subseteq A$ be an ideal, and let $D(A)$ be the derived category of $A$-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Assume that $A[0]$ is derived complete with respect to $I$ [def-weil-point-derived-complete-module-complex]. Then every perfect $P\in D(A)$ [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex], meaning an object isomorphic to a bounded complex of finitely generated projective $A$-modules, is derived complete with respect to $I$.

source.place: Tag 091S, definition-derived-complete and the immediately following assertion that D_comp(A,I) is strictly full, saturated and triangulated; Tag 0ATI, lemma-perfect-ring-classical-generator

proof.text: Let $\mathcal C$ be the full subcategory of $D(A)$ consisting of objects derived complete with respect to $I$. The hypothesis places $A[0]$ in $\mathcal C$. Derived completeness is an object property defined by vanishing of the multiplication-tower derived limits, so it is invariant under isomorphism; hence $\mathcal C$ is strictly full. The zero object is complete because every multiplication tower on it is zero.

source.place: Tag 091S, Definition 15.93.4 and the immediately following assertion that the derived-complete subcategory is strictly full

proof.text: The existing closure theorem [lem-weil-pbc-module-derived-complete-products-triangles] says that in any distinguished triangle, if two objects are derived $I$-complete then so is the third. Together with the distinguished triangle $X\to0\to X[1]\to X[1]$ and its rotations supplied by the triangulated axioms [def-weil-triangulated-category], and the zero-object observation of Step 1, this makes $\mathcal C$ closed under all shifts and under cones; thus $\mathcal C$ is triangulated.

source.place: Tag 091S, assertion that derived-complete objects form a triangulated subcategory

proof.text: Let $K\in\mathcal C$ and let $i:P\to K$, $r:K\to P$ satisfy $r\circ i=\mathrm{id}_P$. Fix $f\in I$ and $q\in\mathbf Z$. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-localization-tower-vanishing] and [def-weil-point-derived-complete-module-complex], every morphism $A_f[0][q]\to K$ is zero. For any $a:A_f[0][q]\to P$, therefore $i\circ a=0$ and $a=r\circ i\circ a=0$. Applying the same equivalence to every multiplication-tower derived limit of $P$ gives that $P$ is derived complete. Thus $\mathcal C$ is closed under retracts and is saturated (Stacks Tag 091S).

source.place: Tag 091P, lemma-hom-from-Af, (1) iff (3); Tag 091S, definition-derived-complete and following saturation assertion

proof.text: By [lem-sf-perfect-ring-classical-generator] (Tag 0ATI), the full subcategory of perfect objects is the smallest strictly full, saturated, triangulated subcategory of $D(A)$ containing $A[0]$. Since $\mathcal C$ has these closure properties and contains $A[0]$ by hypothesis, every perfect object lies in $\mathcal C$. Using [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex], this applies to every object isomorphic to a bounded complex of finitely generated projective $A$-modules, proving the claim.
